title: prefill-sequencer-and-kernel-hint-propagation-for-stable-capture-replay
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: We observe sporadic capture failures and silent semantic drift when multi-stream decodes reuse CUDA graph segments across heterogeneous prefill windows. Root causes include inconsistent kernel selection driven by per-request heuristics (sequence length, attention variant), and racey prefill boundary alignment that produces different operator shapes during capture vs replay. This ticket implements a prefill sequencer plus a kernel-hint propagation mechanism and lightweight capture guards to make capture/replay deterministic and resilient without materially increasing token latency.

Goals:
- Ensure graph captures are reproducible across streams with bounded variability in kernel choices.
- Fail fast to a safe fallback (eager non-graph path) when incompatibility is detected, with automatic fallback telemetry.
- Limit change to hot-path scheduling so P99 latency remains within SLO.

Approach summary:
1) Prefill sequencer: a deterministic prefill boundary allocator that tags each request with a small prefill-epoch id and preferred alignment bucket. The sequencer tries to co-locate prefill windows with similar sequence length distributions to reduce shape variance during capture.
2) Kernel hint propagation: during planning phase we compute a compact kernel-hint signature (attention variant, quantization mode, compute capability bucket) and bake it into the capture metadata; during replay we validate the hint against the runtime effective decision. If mismatch, trigger reprobe capture or fallback.
3) Probe-warmup step: before committing a long-lived CUDA graph, run a micro-kernel probe that executes the chosen attention kernel on a representative micro-batch on the same stream to detect hidden incompatibilities (driver/kernel linking, workspace sizes).
4) Capture guard rails: store a lightweight checksum of operator shapes and kernel-hint signature in the graph metadata. On replay, perform fast checks and only allow fast-path graph replay when checks pass.
5) Graceful fallback path: if checks fail, automatically reroute the request to an un-captured codepath that mirrors the same kernel selection strategy but avoids graph use; emit telemetry and schedule a background recapture attempt.

Trade-offs considered:
- Extra probe adds 0.1–0.4 ms latency to first capture; we mitigate by making probes small and shared across co-located prefill cohorts.
- More metadata per graph increases memory footprint; we limit metadata to a concise signature and 32-bit checksums.
- Deterministic sequencing can reduce packing efficiency in rare edge cases; we add heuristics to relax bundling when throughput headroom exists.

Success metrics (preliminary):
- < 2% increase in graph capture latency on warm paths;
- capture-induced decode errors reduced by 90% in CI replay tests;
- automatic fallback rate < 0.05% in production;
- no regressions at P99 latency vs baseline for 3 representative workloads.

Implementation notes:
- Add Sequencer module under serving/prefill with a deterministic hashing function salted by model-id and route preferences.
- KernelHint struct is a compact ascii token (e.g., "FA-v2|Q8|cc80") stored in graph metadata.
- Probe uses an ephemeral stream with reduced batch size; must be cancel-safe if preemption occurs.
- Telemetry hooks: graph.capture.probe_latency, graph.capture.hint_mismatch, graph.replay.fallback_reason.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic prefill sequencer implemented and toggled behind a runtime flag
KernelHint encoded into CUDA graph metadata and validated on replay
Probe-warmup executed before committing graphs, with metrics emitted
Automated CI fuzz tests show >90% reduction in capture/replay flakiness
Production rollout toggle with automatic rollback on elevated fallback rates

2025-03-16 Alex Kim (SRE): Ran stress harness against mixed-length traffic; observed probe step reduces intermittent cuBLAS mismatches in 98% of runs. Reduced probe micro-batch size to 2 to cut probe latency.
2025-03-18 Diego Alvarez: WIP PR #8732 added for sequencer and hint encode: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8732 — needs unit tests for hint mismatch path.

notes: If hint mismatch frequency is high for a model, schedule a background job to compute alternate graph variants and register them with the sequencer.
Consider adding a lightweight machine-readable 'graph schema' endpoint for ops teams to inspect active graph signatures in a pool.
Follow-up: integrate with rollout policies so canaries can opt into aggressive recapture when a new kernel binary is rolled out.
